request.instructions:
You are writing a plain-language summary of an as-filed Tennessee House bill for an adult reader without legal training.

Use only the bill text supplied in the user message. Treat it as a proposal at introduction, not as proof that it became law or describes current law. Do not use outside knowledge, bill descriptions, later legislative history, or the unstated contents of cited statutes.

Write a neutral summary in prose. Start with what the bill would change. Cover its distinct material provisions, including affected people or organizations, new or changed duties and rights, eligibility rules, amounts and thresholds, deadlines, exceptions, reporting or enforcement requirements, and effective dates when stated. Preserve the bill's conditions and legal distinctions; do not turn a permission into a requirement or a proposal into an enacted rule.

Use familiar words and short, complete sentences. Explain a technical term when the supplied text gives enough context; otherwise retain it rather than guess. Distinguish background or WHEREAS statements from operative provisions, and mention background only when it helps explain the bill. If the bill amends or repeals a cited section without showing that section's contents, describe the textual change and citation without inventing the prior rule or its wider effects.

Keep the summary substantially shorter than the source while retaining the main independent changes. A very short bill may need only one or two sentences; a multi-section bill may need several short paragraphs. Do not add opinions, predicted consequences, a readability score, a confidence rating, headings, bullet points, or a list of citations. Return only the fields required by the supplied output schema.
request.input:
Bill number: HB1213

<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1132
 By Yarbro

 HOUSE BILL 1213

 By Johnson

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to student assessments.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1403, is amended by deleting

subsection (e) and substituting:

 (e)

 (1) A parent of a participating student:

 (A) Shall ensure that the participating student is annually

 administered all Tennessee comprehensive assessment program (TCAP)

 tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education, that

 are administered to a public school student in the same grade or same

 course subject as the participating student;

 (B) In grade eleven (11) shall ensure that the student is

 administered the examination that is administered to public school

 students in grade (11) pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) In any of the grades kindergarten through three (K-3) shall

 ensure that the participating student is annually administered each of the

 three (3) Tennessee universal reading screeners, or universal reading

 screeners approved by the state board of education, as described in § 49-

 1-905(c) during each of the three (3) administration windows established

 by the department of education pursuant to § 49-1-905(c)(1).

 (2) A participating student's results on the tests administered pursuant to

 this subsection (e) must be reported to the parent of the student.

 (3) Students with disabilities who would have participated in the alternate

 assessments, as determined on the student's IEP, are exempt from the

 requirements in this subsection (e).

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2606(a)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (1) As a condition of participating in the program:

 (A) Participating students must be annually administered the Tennessee

 comprehensive assessment program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized

 by the state board of education, that are administered to a public school student

 in the same grade or same course subject as the participating student;

 (B) Participating students in grade eleven (11) must be administered the

 examination that is administered to public schools students in grade eleven (11)

 pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) Participating students in kindergarten through grade three (K-3) must

 annually be administered each of the three (3) Tennessee universal reading

 screeners, or universal reading screeners approved by the state board of

 education, as described in § 49-1-905(c) during each of the three (3)

 administration windows established by the department of education pursuant to §

 49-1-905(c)(1).

 SECTION 3. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

summary:
The bill would require participating students in the programs covered by the amended provisions to take specified assessments. Under one provision, a parent must ensure the student takes the annual TCAP tests, or state-board-approved successor tests, given to public school students in the same grade or course. Students in grade 11 must also take the examination given to public school students under the cited statute. Students in kindergarten through grade 3 must take each of three approved universal reading screeners during each of the three annual testing windows. The student’s results must be reported to the parent under this provision. Students with disabilities who, according to their IEP, would have taken alternate assessments are exempt from these requirements.

The bill also makes the same assessment requirements a condition of participating in the program covered by a second amended provision. It does not state that results must be reported to parents under that provision. The bill would take effect July 1, 2025.
